form: A single tall Art Nouveau courtroom built after Mucha, oak-panelled in flowing carved curves under an open timber roof of curved gilded braces: a raised royal bench and double throne at one end under a canopy, a raised jury-box of two tiers down one side, the dock opposite, a table with a dish of tarts in the very middle of the floor, the crowd standing on the floor and in a shallow gallery at the back
culture_ref: geography.json#LOC-courtroom, LOC-courthouse; world.json#wonderland_real_counterparts cp-court; culture.json CUL-006, CUL-007, CUL-011, CUL-016, CUL-040
period: Dream-image of an 1860s English assize court as a well-read child pictures it from books and newspaper engravings (wig and bench, jury-box, herald; the royal arms swapped for the arms of Hearts), its architecture redrawn in the dream's licensed Art Nouveau language (WR-010); costumes and hand props stay 1862

grows_from.waking_detail: a court of justice Alice has only read about in books: judge's wig, jury-box, herald
grows_from.design_growth: The courtroom of a book illustration and of the Oxford county courts in their castle-style Gothic Revival hall (built 1841; the waking source only, its architecture redrawn in the dream's Art Nouveau), assembled from the names Alice is proud to know: 'judge', 'jury-box', 'jurors'. Each named thing is slightly too large and too prominent, as if labelled; the judge's bench has become a throne, and the court's floor comes out as a mosaic in the court's own colours, red, black and buff, softened with cream and gold

dream_design_language: Solemn authority redrawn as a Mucha poster built in oak, glass and iron: dark oak panels carved in flowing whiplash lines, tall round-headed stained-glass windows, the throne set against a great circular stained-glass halo roundel so the King and Queen sit like figures in a Mucha panel. Floor mosaic, canopy and carved panels repeat hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades entwined with rose and vine ornament. Cast-iron gallery front of organic whiplash scrolls with verdigris and traces of gilding. Palette: dark oak and crimson grounded, pastel glass and gold above

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau: flowing organic line in all joinery and ironwork, rose-and-vine ornament wound through the card-suit motifs, circular halo roundel behind the throne, mosaic floor, stained glass in every window, pastel-and-gold light over dark oak
mucha_design_language.culture_ref: world.json#WR-010 (the court listed); cultivation.json#XA-magic-08; refs/style/alice.jpeg (ironwork, stained glass)
mucha_design_language.why: Replaces the former 1850s-60s Gothic Revival translation; built as a photographed physical set

structure.item: one hall about 20 m long by 13 m wide, walls panelled in oak to 3 m, plastered above, open oak roof on curved, gilded Art Nouveau braces with the ridge about 11 m high
structure.why: Period assize-court proportions; room for 'a great crowd'

structure.item: at the north end, a raised royal bench on a dais of three steps (about 1.2 m high) with a double throne where the King and Queen of Hearts sit, under a crimson canopy
structure.note: 'seated on their throne'; dais and canopy inferred from a judge's bench

structure.item: the jury-box down the east wall: an oak enclosure with two tiers of six seats, its floor raised about 1.2 m above the court floor so the crowd stands below it; each seat carries a raised cushioned perch-block so the small CGI animal jurors (SUP-002 as amended BIB-0027) sit with heads above the ledge
structure.note: twelve jurors; the raised floor follows ch012-p01 'upsetting all the jurymen on to the heads of the crowd below'; perch-block height to match 04-creatures juror sizes

structure.item: the dock opposite on the west side: a low oak enclosure with an iron rail where the Knave stands in chains between two soldiers
in the very middle of the floor a table with a large dish of tarts on it
a witness stand beside the table on the jury side, a small raised oak box with a rail
structure.note: the Hatter as first witness; stand inferred from court procedure (culture.json CUL-006)

structure.item: the herald's place just below and beside the King's end of the bench, where the White Rabbit (photoreal CGI rabbit) stands on a low oak step with trumpet and scroll
the open floor of the court filled by the standing crowd (little CGI birds and beasts among the card figures), and a shallow raised public gallery across the south end over the entrance
structure.note: 'a great crowd assembled about them'; gallery inferred from period courts

structure.item: the main entrance door in the south wall under the gallery, where the crowd sneezes as the cook arrives and the Hatter escapes

materials.item: dark varnished oak for panelling, bench, jury-box, dock, stand and roof timbers, carved in flowing Art Nouveau curves
materials.why: Court joinery kept dark and heavy; its line is the dream's Art Nouveau

materials.item: mosaic floor of small stone and glass tesserae: flowing rose-and-vine borders in cream and gold framing fields of red, black and buff, with inset heart, diamond, club and spade roundels
materials.culture_ref: culture.json CUL-016 (court organised as a deck of cards); world.json#WR-010 (mosaic)
materials.why: Mosaic is a WR-010 accent; keeps the card court's colours

materials.item: cream lime plaster above the panelling
materials.why: Lets the windows and roof read

materials.item: crimson wool damask for the throne canopy and the bench front hangings, with a gold fringe
materials.why: The court's colour at the focal end

materials.item: cast-iron gallery front of organic whiplash scrolls and lily stems, dark green with verdigris and traces of old gilding
materials.why: The style reference's aged Art Nouveau ironwork, now licensed in the dream

details.item: the arms of Hearts carved and painted above the throne canopy: a shield with a single red heart, crowned
details.why: Replaces the royal arms that hang over every real English bench

details.item: twelve small slates and slate-pencils on the jury-box ledge (props owned by 06-art/prop)
oak panels carved with the four card suits in low relief, each suit caught in a flowing frame of rose stems and vine tendrils
details.why: Carries the card motif into the Art Nouveau ornament

details.item: a brass rail along the jury-box front and a hinged oak door at its end
details.why: Period jury-box fittings; the rail is what Alice's skirt catches

details.item: a great circular stained-glass halo roundel in the north wall above the throne canopy: one red heart at the centre, radiating petals of pastel rose, lilac and gold glass in lead came
details.culture_ref: culture.json CUL-016; world.json#WR-010 (halo roundel, stained glass)
details.why: Mucha's halo behind the enthroned figures, carrying the court's emblem

interior.layout: Rectangle 20 x 13 m, long axis north-south. North end: dais and double throne under canopy, herald's place at its east corner, stained-glass halo roundel above. East wall: raised two-tier jury-box (floor +1.2 m), witness stand just south of it. West wall: dock with rail. Centre of the floor: the table with the dish of tarts. South end: shallow public gallery over the main door. Crowd stands on the open floor between the table, the dock and the jury-box
openings: east wall: three tall round-headed stained-glass windows above the panelling (pale pastel floral glass, mostly clear-toned so daylight passes), sills at 4 m, over the jury-box
west wall: three matching tall round-headed stained-glass windows above the panelling, sills at 4 m, over the dock
north wall: one circular stained-glass halo roundel, about 3.5 m across, above the throne canopy (red heart centre)
south wall: main double doors under the gallery, 2.8 m high, opening inward
north-east corner: a small door behind the dais for officers of the court
interior.furniture_tone: Solemn, heavy, dark oak and crimson below; pastel glass and gold above; everything built to impress a child with the weight of adult procedure

scale_notes.rule: Alice grows during the trial (ch011-p29 to ch012-p63) as she stops deferring to the court. Main set at 1:1 for the opening (Alice 135 cm among the crowd, looking up at the throne and the raised jury-box). For the grown shots build a second 2/3-scale version of the jury-box corner and dais (jury-box rail at 70 cm instead of 1.05 m, throne dais 80 cm) with scaled doubles for the card figures and the CGI animal jurors re-scaled to match, so Alice at true height towers over it. The tipping of the jury-box (ch012-p01) uses a lightweight breakaway jury-box on its raised platform; the CGI jurors tumble onto the crowd below (card-figure performers on padding, CGI small animals). Final beat (ch012-p63, 'grown to her full size') is shot on the 2/3 set so the whole pack is below her eye line before it rises and flies at her
scale_notes.feeling: Size tracks authority: small and awed on entering, towering and fearless at 'You're nothing but a pack of cards!'
scale_notes.why: The text gives growth without figures; a two-thirds build keeps the card-figure performers human-sized (SUP-004) while making the growth legible

negative: no modern courtroom: no microphones, no electric lights, no strip lighting, no modern flags
no gallows, block, axe or any execution apparatus anywhere in the room
no fantasy throne room, no palace columns, no castle hall
no cartoon animals, no humans in animal costume; animal jurors and crowd animals are photoreal CGI animals, card figures are human performers
no Art Deco, no Gothic pointed lancets or tracery; no flat poster illustration, outline graphics or matte-painting finish
no playing-card graphics printed flat on walls; suit motifs only carved, in mosaic or in glass
prompt_ready_en: a tall Art Nouveau courtroom in the style of Alphonse Mucha built as a real set, dark oak panelling carved in flowing whiplash curves with card suits entwined in rose and vine ornament, an open timber roof on curved gilded braces, tall round-headed pastel stained-glass windows, at the far end a double throne on a raised dais under a crimson damask canopy with a crowned red-heart shield, backed by a great circular stained-glass halo roundel with a red heart at its centre, a raised two-tier oak jury-box along one side with slates on its ledge, an oak dock with an iron rail opposite, a table with a large dish of tarts in the middle of a mosaic floor of red black and buff with cream and gold vine borders, a verdigris cast-iron gallery of organic scrolls over the entrance
